chapter: Portraits from Hemphill to Getz, and the bebop question
title: Stuff Smith could talk while playing; Horace and Fletcher couldn't
summary: Stuff Smith came from Alphonso Trent's band and chatted with the audience while playing; Horace, Fletcher, Erroll Garner and Earl Hines cannot talk and play.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: You were just telling me a little bit about t Stuff Smith and his ability to talk while he was playing.
Oh, yes. Well, you know, Stuff Smith came from a great band Ant named Alphonso Trent. This is quite a few years back, but he had a swinging band. Stuff

was a member of that band, and he had two excellent saxopho- nists, one named Jeter Creater and the other named Pillars, which later they founded a band called the Jeter-Pillars aggregation, which played in St. Louis and Kansas City. But getting back to Stuff, I used to notice Stuff when he was performing. Stuff could play his fiddle and would be playing all those riffs and would be talking to people in the audience. Tom, I can't talk and play.
(Laughter)
I know --
I really can't
-- what you mean.

I found out that you can't either be the -- but that comes from, I guess, you know, you have to concentrate on your keys and whatnot. Even now, here something happened was real funny at a job that I played about a month ago. There was a guy came up, and he wanted to talk to me, and it seemed like he waited just the time before the organ solo and It was about to happen. He came up and he wanted me to talk. So one of the musicians in my band knew that it was pretty hard for me to talk and play, so he said, 'Mister, why don't you wait until he finishes his solo?' Well, the guy didn't know what he meant, 'finishes his solo?' and things, you know?
Yeah.

He said, 'Well, I mean he can't talk and play. Why don't you wait?' He says, 'Wait, I'll prove something to you.' So he walked over to me while I was playing, and he said, 'Is it all right if I get a hammer and take you out and beat you on the head when you get through, so you -- and I would shake my head, yes. I don't know what he said, you know.
(Laughter)

And he said, 'See what I mean?' So when we got through, he says, 'Do you know what I said to you?' I says, 'No.' So he told the guy, 'See what I mean?' So the guy understood, and he thought it was funny.
(Laughter)

But those things happen. But getting back to Stuff, Stuff could walk through the audience and holler over to a guy, want to know what time the restaurants close and all this thing, and at the same time, man, he's playing some classics, so they're just moving. I can't -- I don't know how the guy could do it. I know a lot of guys can do this. But do you know the answer to that?
I sure don't. I really don't. I can say that I know many pianists that can do it. Could Fletcher? Do you recall?
Do you know, just reminiscing a little bit, Fletcher couldn't talk either. I remember people
talking to him, and he'd say, 'Just a minute' or one of those things. I can't even get that out.
(Laughter)
Just a minute, you know?
I stammer.
Yeah, yeah.
Or stutter.
And I'll tell you, I know another guy that could -- an excellent pianist that can't talk, and he's buzzing all the time -- Earl Garner.
Uh-huh. Oh, yeah, he's got all that sound going.

You say something to Earl, he -- he's sawing away, you know, and no way, see. So after I saw, Earl Hines is another one can't talk while he plays, unless he's learned to recently, but I doubt seriously he can because, well, concentration is a hard thing. Sometimes there are people that can do two things at once, but I'm not one of them. No way.
Not I. Not I either.
So I just hold my finger up sometimes and act like I don't hear that person, which I don't. I hear them, and I don't hear them, you know.
Yeah. Well, you hear the sound, but you don't know what he's saying.
I hear them to an extent, but I can't answer them, because I don't know what they're saying. I'm still looking at black and white keys. So this is -- it's one of those things, you know.
